div.div: The re-scan form sweeps the source once per destination segment, so its cost grows with payload/M. Spilling into RAM-sized buckets removes the re-read: the payload crosses scratch once each way and nothing is ever read twice.

f = M / W of them, one container each.
A record goes to the buffer for the
segment its destination falls in.

d = f(s), computed per record.
No inverse table is resident, so nothing
in memory scales with the ordinal count.

one region per bucket. Each is appended
a container at a time and read back

div.div: monotone reads · container-sized appends · contiguous writes · never a backward seek, on either side, in either stage

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 635px; margin-left: 2px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#666666, #959595); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Why one stage is nearly always enough. A bucket is only worth having if its spill writes are large enough not to seek, so each costs a container-sized buffer and
f = M/W is how many a single sweep can keep open. With a 32 GiB budget and 128 KiB containers f is a quarter of a million — a terabyte needs 32 buckets and a
petabyte 32,768, both far inside it. When the segment count does exceed f the split recurses, for ⌈log_f(segments)⌉ stages; growth is logarithmic in how badly
memory is oversubscribed, and the base is enormous.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 715px; margin-left: 2px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#666666, #959595); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
What it costs. 2·(stages + 1) sequential passes over the payload, independent of the segment count — against the re-scan form's A(P) + 1, which is not. The two are
level at four segments: below that the re-scan is genuinely cheaper because it never touches scratch, and above it the gap has no upper end. This is the external
distribution sort of Aggarwal & Vitter's I/O model (Commun. ACM 31(9), 1988); the log_f here is their log_(M/B).
